scope: Isolated Node24 JavaScript Gap versus native Rust Gap. No WASM, CRDT, editor or production integration.

conditions.buildCompilerSource: Native runner owner build command, independently queried stable toolchain version
conditions.optimization: cargo build --release, Cargo profile lto=true codegen-units=1 panic=abort
conditions.concurrency: Sequential child processes; one measured runtime at a time. External machine load not controlled.

algorithm: Initial initialized gap 64; overlapping gap movement; delete before growth; extra=max(required-gap,floor(post-delete logical length/2),64); fresh contiguous output. Rust Vec allocator capacity may differ from initialized units.
timingBoundary: Fresh process per runtime/sample; prepared binary trace parsing and process startup excluded. Five untimed complete warmups in the same process. Construction includes copying initial units. Edit phase includes the runtime native API and validation. Fresh materialization allocates/copies output. Pipeline equals per-sample phase sum. JSON, IPC, independent oracle, hashing, and release excluded.
fairnessLimits: Node JIT/GC versus Rust release compilation; Vec and TypedArray allocators differ. Native runner uses Result/capacity checks and JS uses RangeError/capacity checks. This is bounded storage/runtime comparison, not a language-wide claim.

differential.oracle: Independent UTF-16 JavaScript string slice, each full code unit checked after every operation against both runtimes; status and initialized storage growth parity checked.

memory.method: Fresh separate subprocess per runtime/trace; parent observes ps -o rss= -p PID on Darwin in KiB while child pauses. Baseline is before trace loading. No forced GC. RSS snapshots are total process/runtime plus retained trace, not allocator heap or peak. Adjacent phase deltas are observed changes only. Released drops Gap and materialized output but retains parsed trace; GC/allocator may retain pages. Full-output JSON serialization occurs after materialized snapshot and before released snapshot. Node memoryUsage is supplementary bytes and not a cross-runtime comparator.
